newsitem.title: UK: Freight market quieter, undertone still steady.
newsitem.headline: Freight market quieter, undertone still steady.

text.p: Brokers generally used expressions like 'the market is taking a breather', 'it's pausing' or even 'the fever is over' to describe today's dry cargo conditions.
Despite the BFI scoring another solid gain of 18 points to 1256 - up from 1000 on Oct 1 - some negative factors appeared.

Quite a high number of Panamaxes have failed at the end of this week on subjects, particularly in the Atlantic. The Middle East/S.Africa market was believed by some brokers to have peaked and there were also those who believed North Pacific rates had little further potential improvement. But there were also brokers who claimed the underlying tone of Panamxes was steady.
Brokers said Chinese charterers, for example, were understood to have at least two panamaxes on subjects for fertilizers stems from US Gulf.

There were no fresh reports of period activity except that Madonna Lily 64,747 dwt may have been relet with November delivery Far East for 12 months at $8,500 daily. Meanwhile Capers still seem to be enjoying a revival of fortunes in the East and the Atlantic was more active for these types, although rates have yet to respond decisively.
The North Atlantic was generally healthy for Handy-sizes but in other areas there was little change.
GRAIN - Cargill paid a firmer equivalent of $15.80 for Narwal for 52,000 grains 53' from Plate and Brazil to Continent for Oct/Nov (last fixed Alabacore at $3.75 a week ago).
Cargill were linked with Konavle for 60,000 heavy grain US Gulf to the Continent for Nov 10/15 at $13.50 but doubts were expressed that this was reliable.

In fact some observers considered the current market in this trade was nearer $13.00 than $13.50 for heavy grain despite rumours Itochu had booked Atlantic Prestige for 59,000 tonnes to Hamburg for Oct/Nov at $12.00.
Dreyfus were rumoured to have covered 52-54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for Dec at $23.00 no combo.

In the east Continental fixed Oakby 64,197 dwt delivery Japan end Oct trip via Australia to Aqaba at $10,000 daily, having previously taken Caravos Trader 52,630 delivery spot N.China trip via Nopac to Trincomalee at $7,400 daily.
Handy business included Andre's fixtures of 20,000 wheat St Lawrence/Casablanca for Oct/Nov at $15.60 and 21,700/24,200 S. Australia/Durban for early nov at close to $16.00.
Sometra fixed privately from N.France to W.Africa and CNAN took Rio Madeira 23,851 dwt on subjects delivery Conakry for a trip via US Gulf to algeria at $5,500 daily.
MINERALS/FERTILISERS - China Steel and Posco booked Caper units in the Pacific and Eden 138,000 was understood covered on timecharter delivery China end Nov for the Posco coal tender.

Port Line were rumoured to have fixed a Caper for coal from Richards Bay to Sines for Dec 16/31 at $5.65 but size and name of vessel were not available. The 1982-built Marine Courage 139,000 dwt was reported taken by Pan Ocean ddelivery Ijmuiden early Dec for 13/15 months at $10,100/$10,200 daily.

Market rumours suggested Chinese charterers were active in the US Gulf covering Panamaxes for fertilizers. Lia M 75,453 dwt and Darya Geeth 73,236 dwt were mentioned as having fixed unknown business on subjects.
British steel covered 70,000 iron ore Almeria/Port Talbot on a prompt basis at between $4.00 and $4.50. Maja Vestida 70,213 dwt was believed fixed for a Transatlantic round.
Cargill were firm at $31.00 for 30,000 fertilisers Tampa/Karachi compared to last fixed $29.75 but were said not to be seeing tonnage at much less than $35.00.

Among vessels which failed on subjects with Noble were Giovanni Bottiglieri 73,000 dwt delivery prompt Continent for fertilizers from Us Gulf to China at $13,000 daily and Hua Kai 64,649 dwt delivery Zhanjiang for a West Australian iron ore round at $7,100 daily.
